actualIndependentReview.summary: Viewed the actual 128px portrait and all 18 poses at native 1x and nearest 3x on the supplied light, dark and checker PNGs. The wingless coil, long muzzle, whisker, blue mane and pale icy material read clearly; broad upper-left highlights and lower-right teal shadows give useful volume. The body occupies the cell well and its coil maintains a ground contact. No obvious unintended transparent puncture or wholly detached anatomical part is visible. The main visual weakness is forelimb anatomy: a tiny bent limb beside the upright torso becomes difficult to reconcile with the large leg-shaped appendage emerging near the coil, and attack exaggerates that appendage into a smooth paddle. The hit neck also pinches into a sharp, visually cut junction. Windup, lowered advance, open-jaw attack, recovery and low collapse are distinguishable. The additional states are distinct authored silhouettes rather than body tints: mouth core, two-branch ice breath and three recovery shards; hunched poison with green bubbles; slumped stun with stars; closed-eye sleep with small posture changes. The skill breath visibly starts inside the actual mouth. Review recommendation only; the user's selection remains separate. These static previews cannot establish animation timing, sliding/contact in battle, runtime effect alignment, or literal-grid authorship, and a geometry PASS would not resolve the anatomical concerns.

issues.message: The small bent limb beside the torso and the much larger appendage rooted around (77,93) do not read as a consistent pair of two short dragon forelegs. Redraw their shoulder roots at coherent positions on the upper body, give both an identifiable upper arm/elbow/paw, and shorten the long leg-shaped appendage. Preserve those attachment landmarks in idle_b/c and the action poses.

The vertical throat ends against the diagonal chest through a pinched border junction, producing a cut-neck impression at 1x. Broaden the join around x44-51, y64-70 with a continuous band of neck midtone and shadow, then carry the throat highlight into the recoiling chest curve. Preserve the recoil while removing the sharp anatomical discontinuity.

The attacking appendage expands into a long broad paddle with a rounded mitten end, losing the short clawed foreleg identity established by the idle's small limb. Keep its shoulder and elbow consistent with move/windup, shorten the broad shaft, and articulate two or three claw tips in the outer paw contour around x99-109, y108-113. Carry the same paw proportions into recover and skill poses.
